title: Natural locally constant model of the constant module sheaf
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and let $R$ be a ring. On the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], the functor taking an $R$-module $M$ to the presheaf $W\mapsto\operatorname{LocallyConstant}(|W|,M)$, with restrictions by precomposition and coefficient maps by postcomposition, is naturally isomorphic to the underlying presheaf of the constant module sheaf functor [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. No finiteness, nonzero-ring, or nonemptiness hypotheses are needed.

proof.text: Give the coefficient module the discrete topology. Identify locally constant functions with continuous functions. The already proved Scheme.Etale.continuousMapSheaf is a sheaf of abelian groups; composition with its forgetful functor gives a sheaf of sets. The forgetful functor from ModuleCat preserves and reflects the required limits, so Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp proves the module presheaf is a sheaf.

The natural map from the constant presheaf sends m to its constant function. It is locally surjective by restricting a section to its open fibers; these open immersions are etale and jointly cover. It is locally injective because distinct constants agreeing as functions force the object to be empty, where the empty covering suffices.

Lift that map across sheafification. The unit of sheafification is locally bijective. The composite is the locally bijective map just proved, so the lift is locally bijective and hence an isomorphism by Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso. Use sheafify_hom_ext and toSheafify_naturality to check naturality in each linear coefficient map: both composites send m to the constant function with value its image. Invert this natural isomorphism to obtain the asserted direction.
